turns.prompt_text: Okay so I have three different credit cards I can go with. I have the American Express golden. I have the American Express for grocery and I have a Chase Sapphire preferred. I'm not sure which one I want to use at Ikea
turns.response_html:
Since IKEA doesn't fall into the standard "Grocery" or "Dining" bonus categories for these cards (it's typically coded as a Furniture Store), your decision comes down to the base earn rate and any active "Amex Offers."

Here is the breakdown of how your cards will likely perform at IKEA:

1. The Amex "Gold" (American Express® Gold Card)

  • Base Reward: 1x Membership Rewards point per $1.
  • Why choose this? Only if you have a specific Amex Offer for IKEA. Check your Amex app; there have been recent "targeted" offers for 15% back (up to a certain limit) or bonus points for IKEA purchases. Without an offer, this is your weakest choice for raw value.

2. The Amex "For Grocery" (likely Blue Cash Everyday® or Preferred)

  • Base Reward: 1% Cash Back.
  • The "Online" Catch: If you are shopping on IKEA.com (or using the app for "Click & Collect"), the Blue Cash Everyday® earns 3% back on U.S. online retail purchases (up to $6,000 per year).
  • Why choose this? If you're buying online or in the app, the 3% back is the clear winner. If you're shopping in-store, it's just 1%.

3. Chase Sapphire Preferred®

  • Base Reward: 1x Ultimate Rewards point per $1.
  • The "Portal" Strategy: If you shop through the Shop Through Chase portal before buying online, you can often earn an extra 1–2 points per dollar.
  • Why choose this? If you value Chase points more than Amex points for travel, or if you can stack a portal bonus for an online order.

Quick Comparison Table

CardIn-Store RewardOnline/App RewardBest For...
Amex Gold1x Points1x PointsStacking a targeted "Amex Offer."
Amex Grocery (BCE)1% Cash Back3% Cash BackOnline orders/App purchases.

My Recommendation:

  1. Check your Amex Offers first. If you have a "15% back at IKEA" offer on your Gold or Grocery card, use that—it beats every other reward rate.
  2. Shopping Online? Use the Amex Grocery card (if it's the Blue Cash Everyday) for that 3% back.
  3. Shopping In-Store? Use whichever card you are currently trying to hit a "Minimum Spend" on for a sign-up bonus. If you aren't chasing a bonus, they are all roughly equal (1% or 1x point), so use your favorite points currency.

Note: If you eat at the IKEA Swedish Restaurant, it sometimes codes as "Dining," which would give you 4x points on the Amex Gold or 3x points on the Chase Sapphire Preferred.

turns.prompt_text: I also have this Scheels card. It's a Visa. I have a Home Depot card. I'm a Bass Pro shops card and I have a Michael's card
turns.response_html:
Adding these cards to the mix actually simplifies things because two of them won't work at all, and the others are likely "locked" into rewards you might not want to use at IKEA.

Here is the breakdown of your new options:

1. The "No-Go" Cards

The Home Depot and Michael's cards are "closed-loop" store cards. This means they don't have a Visa or Mastercard logo and cannot be used anywhere except those specific stores.

  • Home Depot Card: Only works at Home Depot.
  • Michael's Card: Only works at Michael's.

2. Scheels Visa & Bass Pro Shops CLUB Card

Since these are Visa and Mastercard, they will work at IKEA, but they aren't your best bet for value:

  • Scheels Visa: You’ll earn 1 point per $1 (1%), but those points can only be redeemed as Scheels Gift Cards. Unless you have a major purchase coming up at Scheels, this is less flexible than cash or travel points.
  • Bass Pro Shops CLUB: You’ll earn 1% back in CLUB points. Again, these points are "locked" into the Bass Pro/Cabela’s ecosystem.

The Updated Verdict: Which should you use?

If you are standing in an IKEA right now, here is your hierarchy of choice:

  1. Winner (Online/App): Amex Grocery (if it's the Blue Cash Everyday). If you use the IKEA app to pay or order online, that 3% cash back is the highest guaranteed return you have across all these cards.
  2. Runner Up (In-Store): Chase Sapphire Preferred or Amex Gold. Both give you 1x point. These points are "transferable" (to airlines/hotels), making them worth more than a standard 1% cash back or a 1% store credit at Scheels/Bass Pro.
  3. Last Resort: Scheels or Bass Pro. Use these only if you are desperately trying to earn enough points for a specific item at those stores (like a new fishing reel or a pair of boots).

One Final Tip: Check your Chase app or Amex app one last time for "Merchant Offers." IKEA frequently runs "Spend $100, Get $10 Back" type deals on these cards. If you see one, that card becomes the instant winner regardless of the base points!

Are you planning to buy something large (like a kitchen or a couch), or just doing a quick run for some Swedish meatballs and organizers?

I do have an online order that I made yesterday, and I don't know if I should just scan everything and purchase it online instead of doing it in the store. I don't know.
turns.response_html:
Since you are planning to make multiple trips to fill your vehicle, the best strategy depends on whether you want to prioritize convenience or maximizing your credit card rewards.

Based on your plan and the cards you have, here is the best way to handle this:

1. The "Maximum Rewards" Strategy: Buy Online / In-App

If your Amex "for grocery" card is the Blue Cash Everyday®, it likely earns 3% cash back on U.S. online retail purchases.

  • How to do it: Instead of using the standard checkout lane, use the IKEA app while you are in the store. Many IKEAs allow you to "Scan & Go" or you can simply add the items to your cart in the app and pay digitally.
  • The Benefit: This typically triggers the "Online Retail" category, giving you 3% back. If you pay at the physical register with that same card, you will likely only get 1% back.

2. The "Convenience" Strategy: Stick to the Online Order

If you already have an online order from yesterday, you might want to see if those items can be picked up via Click & Collect.

  • The Benefit: This saves you from wandering the warehouse for the big stuff. You can load those items first, see how much room is left in your vehicle, and then go inside to shop for the smaller "marketplace" items (organizers, kitchenware, etc.) that are easier to tuck into small gaps.

3. The Vehicle Loading Strategy

Since you are trying to see what your vehicle can handle, here is the most efficient workflow:

  • Step 1: Pick up your Online Order first. These are usually your largest or "must-have" items. Load them into the vehicle to establish your "base layer."
  • Step 2: Go inside for the "Filler" trips. Now that you see how much space is left, you can grab the smaller items.
  • Step 3: Pay via the IKEA App. Use your Amex Grocery/Online card or your Amex Gold (if you have an IKEA-specific "Amex Offer" activated) to pay for these smaller batches.

Summary Recommendation:

  • Best Card for the Online/App purchases: Amex Grocery (for that potential 3% "Online Retail" bonus).
  • Best Card for the Swedish Restaurant (Meatballs): Amex Gold (for 4x points on dining) or Chase Sapphire Preferred (for 3x points on dining).
  • Avoid: Using the Scheels, Bass Pro, Home Depot, or Michael's cards. They will either not work or provide much lower value (1%) compared to the travel points or online-retail cash back on your other cards.

Pro-Tip: If you haven't already, sign up for IKEA Family (it’s free). It gives you extra protection if something breaks during transport—which is a real risk when you're "slowly filling up" a vehicle to its absolute limit!

turns.prompt_text: I did sign up for Ikea family. I am I also applied for the credit card. However, I was declined and maybe because I just used the new address in Ames where it's usually I use my address in Ankeny, but I'm not sure if I can try again.
turns.response_html:
The address mismatch is almost certainly what triggered the decline. Credit card issuers like Comenity Bank (who handles IKEA's cards) use automated systems that cross-reference your application against your credit report. If your credit report still has your Ankeny address but you applied with your new Ames address, the system essentially sees a "red flag" for potential identity fraud and defaults to a "No."

Since you just signed your lease in Ames recently, it takes a few months for that new address to "seed" into the credit bureaus via your utility bills or updated bank statements.

How to Fix This (The "Pro" Move)

Don't just re-apply! Doing so immediately will likely result in another automated rejection and a second "hard inquiry" on your credit score for no reason. Instead, try these steps:

  1. Call the Reconsideration Line: Call Comenity Bank's customer service for the IKEA Visa at 1-866-387-6145.

    • What to say: "I recently applied and was declined, but I believe it was due to a recent move and address verification issue. I’d like to speak with a specialist to verify my identity and reconsider the application."
    • The Result: A human can often override the computer if you can prove you are who you say you are (they might ask for a utility bill or just verify your previous Ankeny address).

  2. Wait 30–90 Days: If you don't want to call, wait at least 3 months. In the meantime, update your address with Amex and Chase. Once they report your new Ames address to the credit bureaus, your next application at IKEA is much more likely to sail through.

  3. The "Safe" Address: If you decide to try again sooner, use your Ankeny address on the application (as long as you still have access to mail there). It matches your current "official" credit profile, which usually guarantees a smoother automated approval.

Your Best Game Plan for Today

Since you're already at the store and moving items into your vehicle, don't let the credit card hiccup slow you down. Here is the move:

  • Stick to the Amex "Grocery" Card (for the Online/App stuff): If you pay via the IKEA app, you're likely getting that 3% online retail bonus, which is already a solid win.
  • Use IKEA Family: You already have the membership! Scan your IKEA Family card at checkout. Even without the IKEA credit card, you still get the 90-day "Price Protection" and the "Oops-assurance" (breakage protection during transport), which is huge since you're currently testing the limits of your vehicle's cargo capacity.
  • The Big Purchase: If you're buying a single item over $500, the IKEA card would have offered 0% interest, but unless you were planning to carry a balance, your Chase Sapphire Preferred or Amex Gold are actually better long-term because you're earning flexible travel points instead of "IKEA-only" reward certificates.
